name: Iraq
summary: Formed from three Ottoman provinces under a British mandate; independent in 1932; ruled by Saddam Hussein (1979–2003), then shaken by invasion and civil conflict.

knownFor.label: Marsh Arabs
knownFor.note: Reed-house culture of the southern marshes.

location.value: In the Middle East, centred on the fertile plains of the Tigris and Euphrates (Mesopotamia); about 437,000 km².

terrain.value: Mountains in the north, desert in the west, and marshlands along the Tigris and Euphrates.

climate.value: Mostly hot and arid; cold winters with occasional heavy snow in the northern mountains.

resources.value: Some of the largest oil reserves in the world.

disasters.value: Wide-scale droughts; a prolonged drought since 2020.

urbanisation.value: Baghdad, the capital and largest city, has over 8 million people.

disease.value: Effects of war and sanctions on health.

economicBase.value: Dominated by oil, which provided about 92% of foreign exchange earnings in 2021.

tradeRoutes.value: Most oil exports go through its ports, such as the Al Basrah Oil Terminal.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A federal parliamentary republic under a constitution approved by referendum in 2005.

keyRulers.value: King Faisal I. Abd al-Karim Qasim. Saddam Hussein.

succession.value: Monarchy until the 1958 coup; further coups in 1963 and 1968; a new constitution approved in 2005.

institutions.value: The Council of Representatives; the Kurdistan Regional Government in the north.

stability.value: Revolution (1958); Iran–Iraq War (1980–88); Gulf War (1990–91); the 2003 invasion; war with the Islamic State (2013–17).

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Armed forces rebuilt after the US invasion of 2003 with large amounts of American military aid.

majorWars.value: Iran–Iraq War (1980–88); Gulf War after the invasion of Kuwait (1990–91); Iraq War (2003–11).

territoryChange.value: Status of Kirkuk disputed between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.

alliancesRivals.value: One of the founding members of OPEC.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

religion.value: Mostly Muslim; minorities include Christians, Mandaeans, Yarsanis and Yazidis. Najaf and Karbala are major Shia holy places.

languageWriting.value: Arabic and Kurdish are official; Assyrian, Turkmen and Mandaic are spoken regionally.

artsArchitecture.value: Famous for its maqam music tradition, passed down orally by master singers.

socialStructure.value: Mostly Arab, with Kurds, Turkmens, Yazidis, Assyrians, Armenians and other groups.

dailyLife.value: Apartments and houses; rice, kebab, tea.

neighbours.value: Iran, Turkey, Syria, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait.

ideasReligions.value: Ba’athism: the Ba’ath Party took power in 1968, ruling a one-party state.

colonisation.value: Part of the Ottoman Empire from 1534; British Mandate of Mesopotamia from 1920; independent in 1932.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
